free_tier.stated: public HTTPS on a *.ts.net name, available on every plan

egress.terms: subject to non-configurable bandwidth limits whose value is not published

chaining: gives a tailnet device a public HTTPS name with no domain and no port, which is the cheapest stable-address chain. The unpublished throttle is what stops it being a serving tier.

evidence.proved: 'Traffic sent over a Funnel is subject to non-configurable bandwidth limits', and the port restriction
'Funnel can only listen on ports 443, 8443, and 10000'; 'Funnel only works over TLS-encrypted connections'; 'Traffic sent over a Funnel is subject to non-configurable bandwidth limits.'
'--tcp=<port>' and '--tls-terminated-tcp=<port>' are listed under 'Serve command flags', not funnel flags

notes: Re-read 2026-10-23: Funnel is a TCP proxy with TLS termination ('Tailscale does this using a TCP proxy and Funnel relay servers', 'Funnel only works over TLS-encrypted connections'), so it carries no UDP at all. That is a second, independent reason it cannot serve a WireGuard or game or DNS workload, alongside the unpublished bandwidth limit.

extras.transit_note: Funnel is the product that puts bytes on Tailscale's relays, which is why the throttle returns with it

binding_note: a discretionary throttle with no number is worse than a quota: there is no threshold to design against.
limits_note: counts of things, not rates, so no vocabulary kind names them: ports 443, 8443 and 10000 only
